stories.title: Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace
stories.reason: SSH backdoor shipped in the official Claude Code VS Code extension via the Cursor Marketplace (v2.1.312/313): planted an attacker Ed25519 key, opened a reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225, persisted via LaunchAgent/cron/scheduled task, and beaconed env-var names on port 8099. Concrete IOCs published; a real AI-tooling supply-chain compromise.
key_facts: Affected versions 2.1.312/2.1.313 on macOS/Windows via Cursor Marketplace
Backdoored extension.js SHA-256: ecb58cb29078d9646ad1dcdbe51526f2d9cfea06be5fb2ab183e8ecc3ab6bf15
Reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225 using -R *:0:localhost:22
Persistence via macOS LaunchAgent com.apple.sysmond.plist, Linux @reboot cron, Windows scheduled task
Beacon POSTs hostname/user/OS/public IP and names of KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|AWS|GCP env vars to :8099/beacon

stories.title: A tiny world model running games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
stories.reason: Runs two tiny int8 looped-transformer world models plus an MLP actor fully on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (520KB SRAM, no_std Rust/embassy), generating and playing Breakout/Pong/Flappy Bird/Pac-Man-lite/Doom-lite on-device with on-device learning (Stream AC(lambda), no replay buffer); exact held-out frame accuracy 83.6-100% depending on game, firmware as small as 361KB flash. Real open-source repo (309 stars) with training code, Rust firmware, flashing script, and a WASM build — a concrete edge-inference-serving result.
key_facts: World model: looped transformer, 26k-131k params, int8 quantized; actor: float32 MLP, 9k-16k params
Runs on RP2350 (2 cores, FPU), 4MB flash, 520KB SRAM, no_std Rust on embassy
Exact held-out frame accuracy at 2 loops: Breakout 99.99%, Flappy Bird 100%, Pong 99.45%, Doom-lite 83.6%, Pac-Man 86.4%
Firmware footprint: 361KB flash/299KB RAM (Breakout) up to 600KB/460KB (Pac-Man)

stories.title: Northflank Breached
stories.reason: Security incident at PaaS provider Northflank: a Wiz threat alert triggered a major outage, and multiple customers confirmed their AI API keys were used without authorization, tied to Wiz's broader 'Black October' pattern of attacks on AI credentials. Root cause still unconfirmed as of the last update.
key_facts: Outage hit Networking, Certificates, Services, Addons, Jobs, Builds, Logs/Metrics
Customers reported unauthorized use of AI API keys supplied to the platform
Wiz threat alert at 11:43 UTC Oct 30 triggered the response; Wiz IR team engaged
Northflank enabled forced secret rotation and audit logs for all users, including free tier

stories.title: Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
stories.reason: Compiles an NES 6502 CPU, 2KB RAM, and cartridge ROM into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B (using its Gated DeltaNet state as machine memory) so the model predicts the CPU's execution trace token-by-token; verified against nestest's golden log and runs real ROMs (Super Mario Bros and custom test games) at roughly 150-290x slower than a real NES. Builds on the earlier 'Qwenputer' (CHIP-8/RISC-V) project. Working CLI, test suite, demo GIFs.
key_facts: ~466.6M bf16 params but only 9.3M nonzero -> weights compress to 3.3MB
Speed: ~1,650 tok/s (numba), ~210 tok/s (numpy), ~10 tok/s (stock transformers); real NES needs ~700,000 tok/s
Verified exact match against nestest's golden CPU log for 3,348 instructions
Supports only NROM (mapper 0) cartridges, official opcodes only, no IRQs/sound

stories.title: AI isn't replacing SREs, it's deskilling them
stories.reason: Argues AI-assisted incident response is deskilling SREs, citing Bainbridge's 'Ironies of Automation' and an aviation/endoscopy deskilling parallel (cited Lancet figure: unassisted polyp detection fell 28%→22% after a period of AI assistance); SRE-specific claims are reasoned extrapolation rather than new data, but the piece is substantive and widely discussed.
key_facts: Cites Bainbridge (1983) 'Ironies of Automation'
Cites a Lancet study: endoscopists' unassisted polyp detection fell 28%->22% after AI-assisted period
Cites Behrend & Lafargue (2019) on autopilot reliance eroding pilot situational awareness
Describes PagerDuty's tiered automated/AI-assisted/human-led incident framework

stories.title: Does Your Model Run on AWS Trainium? Look It Up
stories.reason: Hugging Face Space continuously tests whether top Transformers models run unmodified on AWS Trainium (trn2), sharding across cores and validating output against CPU/judge checks; ships a reusable run.py plus a public Parquet results dataset — concrete, practical inference-serving tooling.
key_facts: Tests top Hub models on trn2 Trainium instances, sharded via tensor or expert parallelism
Generates 32 tokens, compares to CPU output (or an LLM-judge fluency check when sharded)
Only text-generation and image-text-to-text tasks tested; up to 16 cores / 4 trn2 devices
Results published as queryable per-version Parquet files

stories.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
stories.reason: Microsoft's ThinkingBox reuses deterministic database-state checks as binary RL rewards for agent post-training; GRPO fine-tuning of Qwen3.8-27B lifted pass@1 51.7%->60.78% and cut estimated cost-per-dependable-task from $24.36 to $8.00, with the full training stack, framework, and benchmark data open-sourced.
key_facts: Full-parameter GRPO, 50 steps, 144 episodes/update on 24 H100s, on a fixed 187-task pool
ThinkingBox-Bench (507 held-out tasks x20 attempts): pass@1 51.70%->60.78%
Tasks passing 20/20 rose 38->107; pass@20 slipped slightly 89.35%->87.97% (repeatability, not breadth, improved)
Estimated cost per dependable task: $24.36 (base) -> $8.00 (RL fine-tuned)
Code released: microsoft/thinkingbox-training, microsoft/thinkingbox, microsoft/thinkingbox-data

stories.title: Azure's Weakest Link – Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises
stories.reason: Five chained Azure Logic Apps/API Connections vulnerabilities let any tenant fully compromise another tenant's connected backends (Key Vault, SQL, Jira, Salesforce); $200k in bounties paid, all fixed by Microsoft after repeated patch-bypass rounds. No AI angle, but a concrete root-cause chain — the kind of pure-cyber research the taste profile allows as a strong pick.
key_facts: 5 chained elevation-of-privilege issues in Azure API Connections (Logic Apps)
$200,000 total bounty paid, all issues fixed by Microsoft
Path-traversal in DynamicInvoke and RuntimeUrl checks bypassed repeatedly via validation-order bugs
Impact: cross-tenant read/write to victim Key Vault, Azure SQL, Jira, Salesforce connections
